faqs.question: What is the best treatment for neuropathy?
faqs.answer: The best treatment depends on the cause. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, Dr. Yuvraj Lahre first identifies the underlying cause (diabetes, vitamin deficiency, autoimmune disease, etc.) and treats it. Symptom management includes specialized nerve pain medications (gabapentinoids, TCAs, SNRIs), topical treatments, and lifestyle guidance. Treating the cause plus symptoms gives the best results.

faqs.question: Can neuropathy be reversed?
faqs.answer: Whether neuropathy can be reversed depends on the cause and duration. Neuropathy from vitamin B12 deficiency or well-controlled diabetes can improve significantly once the underlying problem is corrected. Nerve damage from chronic, long-standing conditions may be managed rather than fully reversed — but symptoms can be effectively controlled, and progression can be halted.

faqs.question: What tests are done for neuropathy diagnosis?
faqs.answer: Dr. Yuvraj Lahre performs nerve conduction studies and a detailed neurological examination at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care. Blood tests for underlying causes (diabetes, vitamin levels, thyroid, autoimmune markers) are coordinated. In select cases, nerve biopsy or advanced imaging may be arranged.

whatIsIt: Peripheral neuropathy is a widespread neurological condition caused by damage to the peripheral nerve network—the extensive system that relays messages between your brain, spinal cord, and the rest of your body. When these delicate nerves are injured, the signal transmission is disrupted, often resulting in sensations of pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness, primarily starting in the hands and feet. In Jharkhand, we see many cases stemming not just from poorly controlled diabetes (the most common cause globally), but also from severe vitamin deficiencies and exposure to toxins. By accurately diagnosing the root cause through detailed nerve conduction studies, Dr. Yuvraj Lahre provides targeted therapies at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care to stop further nerve damage and ease debilitating symptoms.
symptoms: A persistent 'pins and needles' sensation or numbness that gradually spreads upward from the toes or fingers
Sharp, stabbing, or intense burning pain, frequently worsening at night
Extreme sensitivity to even light touches, such as the weight of a bedsheet (allodynia)
Muscle weakness, making tasks like gripping objects or walking steadily difficult
A lack of coordination, leading to frequent stumbling or balance issues
Feeling as though you are wearing thick socks or gloves when you are not
In severe cases, autonomic symptoms like dizziness when standing up or digestive issues
causes: Uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, which chronically damages small blood vessels supplying the nerves
Severe nutritional deficits, specifically lacking vital B-vitamins (B1, B6, B12)
Chronic alcohol consumption, leading to toxic nerve damage and poor nutrition
Autoimmune disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, or Guillain-Barré syndrome
Exposure to industrial toxins and heavy metals, a noted risk in some mining areas of Jharkhand
Infections like Lyme disease, shingles, or HIV
Kidney or liver disease causing a buildup of toxins in the bloodstream

diagnosticTests.name: Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS)
diagnosticTests.description: Electrodiagnostic testing that measures how fast and how strongly electrical signals travel through peripheral nerves. Identifies the type (axonal vs. demyelinating) and severity of nerve damage.

diagnosticTests.name: Comprehensive Neurological Examination
diagnosticTests.description: Detailed assessment of sensation, strength, reflexes, and coordination to map the pattern and extent of nerve involvement.

faqs.question: What is the best treatment for carpal tunnel syndrome?
faqs.answer: Treatment depends on severity. Mild to moderate CTS often responds to wrist splinting (especially at night), activity modification, and nerve-gliding exercises. Moderate cases may benefit from corticosteroid injections. Severe or progressive cases with muscle weakness or atrophy may require surgical release. Dr. Yuvraj Lahre evaluates your case and recommends the most appropriate treatment.

faqs.question: Do I need surgery for carpal tunnel syndrome?
faqs.answer: Not always. Many cases of carpal tunnel syndrome improve with conservative (non-surgical) treatment, especially when diagnosed early. Dr. Yuvraj Lahre at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care focuses on accurate diagnosis with nerve conduction studies and starts with medical management. Surgery is considered when conservative measures fail, or when there is significant nerve damage.

faqs.question: How is carpal tunnel syndrome diagnosed?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis involves a detailed history, physical examination (including Tinel's test and Phalen's maneuver), and nerve conduction studies that measure how well the median nerve is functioning. Palamu Neuro & Eye Care has on-site nerve conduction study capability for rapid, accurate diagnosis.

whatIsIt: Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) is a painful compression neuropathy that occurs when the median nerve is squeezed or pinched as it passes through a narrow anatomical tunnel in your wrist. This essential nerve provides feeling to your thumb, index, and middle fingers, as well as controlling the muscles at the base of your thumb. Any condition that causes swelling within this confined space—such as repetitive hand movements, arthritis, or hormonal changes—can trap the nerve. In rural Palamu, we frequently diagnose this in individuals performing heavy, repetitive manual tasks, like traditional grain grinding. Prompt evaluation by Dr. Yuvraj Lahre is critical to relieve the pressure before permanent muscle wasting occurs.
symptoms: Frequent numbness, tingling, or an 'electric shock' feeling in the thumb and first three fingers
Pain or tingling that consistently wakes you up during the night
A tendency to 'shake out' your hands to temporarily relieve the numbness (the flick sign)
Pain radiating up the forearm toward the elbow or shoulder
Noticeable weakness when trying to grip objects, leading to frequently dropping items
Difficulty performing fine motor tasks, like buttoning a shirt or picking up a coin
Visible thinning or flattening of the muscle pad at the base of the thumb (in advanced stages)
causes: Repetitive, high-force flexing or extending of the wrist (e.g., traditional stone grinding, heavy typing)
Anatomical factors, such as naturally having a narrower carpal tunnel
Inflammatory conditions like rheumatoid arthritis causing swelling in the wrist tendons
Fluid retention during pregnancy or menopause, which increases pressure in the tunnel
Metabolic conditions such as diabetes or an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism)
Prior wrist injuries, fractures, or dislocations that altered the tunnel's structure
Obesity, which is statistically linked to a higher risk of developing CTS

diagnosticTests.name: Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS)
diagnosticTests.description: The gold standard diagnostic test. Electrodes measure how fast electrical signals travel through the median nerve across the wrist. Slowing at the carpal tunnel confirms the diagnosis and determines severity.

diagnosticTests.name: Clinical Neurological Examination
diagnosticTests.description: Dr. Lahre performs provocative tests (Tinel's, Phalen's, compression test) and assesses sensation, strength, and muscle bulk in the hands.

treatmentApproach.intro: Dr. Yuvraj Lahre employs a step-wise treatment plan for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome, prioritizing non-surgical interventions:

methods.name: Ergonomic Splinting
methods.description: Prescribing rigid nocturnal wrist splints to keep the joint in a neutral position while sleeping, significantly reducing nighttime nerve compression.

methods.name: Activity Modification
methods.description: Educating patients on modifying repetitive tasks—such as altering grinding techniques or upgrading to motorized tools—and teaching specific nerve-gliding exercises.

methods.name: Medical Intervention
methods.description: Utilizing short courses of anti-inflammatory medications or precisely guided corticosteroid injections directly into the carpal tunnel to rapidly reduce swelling.

methods.name: Surgical Coordination
methods.description: For severe cases showing muscle atrophy on nerve conduction studies, Dr. Lahre coordinates seamless referrals to specialized hand surgeons for a carpal tunnel release.

whenToSeeDoctor: If you have persistent numbness or tingling in your thumb, index, or middle fingers
If your hand symptoms wake you up at night regularly
If you notice weakness in your grip or tendency to drop objects
If your symptoms interfere with work or daily activities
If you see wasting (thinning) of the muscles at the base of your thumb — this indicates advanced nerve damage

clinicalObservations.standardView: Standard medical literature describes carpal tunnel syndrome as a compression neuropathy associated with repetitive hand movements, obesity, diabetes, and pregnancy.
clinicalObservations.palamuObservation: Dr. Yuvraj Lahre at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care sees carpal tunnel disproportionately in women from Palamu's tribal hinterland who spend 6–8 hours daily hand-grinding millets and rice on traditional stone grinders. This repetitive high-resistance motion is biomechanically distinct from the keyboard-related carpal tunnel seen in urban populations.
clinicalObservations.treatmentModification: We explain the mechanism in Hindi, showing patients how the grinding motion compresses the median nerve. For mild cases, night splinting and ergonomic changes to grinding posture often suffice. We recommend motorised grain mills where feasible.

faqs.question: What is endophthalmitis and how serious is it?
faqs.answer: Endophthalmitis is a severe infection of the internal structures of the eye, including the vitreous and/or aqueous humor. It is one of the most serious ophthalmic emergencies — it can cause permanent, severe vision loss or blindness within 24-48 hours if not treated promptly. Immediate specialist eye care is critical.

faqs.question: What are the symptoms of endophthalmitis?
faqs.answer: Symptoms typically include severe eye pain, rapidly worsening vision, intense eye redness, swollen eyelids, sensitivity to light, and sometimes a hypopyon (white fluid level visible behind the cornea). These symptoms demand immediate, emergency ophthalmology evaluation.

faqs.question: How is endophthalmitis treated at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care?
faqs.answer: Treatment must be rapid and aggressive. Dr. Dibya Prabha performs vitreous tap for culture, intravitreal antibiotic injections (delivering medication directly into the eye), and when necessary, emergency vitrectomy surgery to remove infected vitreous and preserve vision. Systemic antibiotics may also be prescribed.

whatIsIt: Endophthalmitis is a devastating, rapidly progressive infection inside the eye, typically involving the vitreous fluid and surrounding tissues. It is considered an absolute ophthalmic emergency. This severe infection most commonly occurs after bacteria or fungi enter the eye during trauma, such as an agricultural injury or an accident involving flying debris without safety goggles—a frequent occurrence in Jharkhand's mining and farming sectors. It can also, though rarely, develop following eye surgery or injections. Without immediate, aggressive intervention by a retina specialist like Dr. Dibya Prabha, the infection can destroy the delicate retinal tissue within hours, resulting in permanent blindness or even the loss of the eye itself.
symptoms: Sudden, excruciating eye pain that worsens rapidly and is disproportionate to the visible injury
A dramatic and fast decline in vision, often leading to only light perception
Severe, diffuse redness over the entire white of the eye
Noticeable swelling of the eyelids and the clear membrane covering the eye (chemosis)
Extreme sensitivity to any light (photophobia)
A visible collection of white or yellowish pus in the lower part of the front of the eye (hypopyon)
A cloudy, hazy appearance to the cornea, obscuring the colored part of the eye
causes: Penetrating eye trauma from flying metal, stone chips, or thorns (highly common in agricultural/mining work)
Post-operative infections following cataract, glaucoma, or retinal surgeries
Infections introduced during intravitreal injections for conditions like macular degeneration
A systemic infection traveling through the bloodstream to the eye (endogenous), often seen in immunocompromised patients
Delayed infection from a previously placed glaucoma drainage device
A severe, unhealed corneal ulcer that perforates into the inner eye chamber
Common pathogens include Staphylococcus, Streptococcus, Pseudomonas, and various fungi

diagnosticTests.name: Immediate Slit-Lamp Examination
diagnosticTests.description: Urgent, detailed examination of the anterior chamber and vitreous for signs of infection — cells, flare, hypopyon, vitritis — to rapidly confirm the clinical diagnosis.

diagnosticTests.name: Vitreous Tap & Culture
diagnosticTests.description: A small sample of vitreous fluid is aspirated and sent for Gram stain, culture, and antibiotic sensitivity testing to identify the causative organism and guide targeted antibiotic therapy.

treatmentApproach.intro: Every hour counts. Dr. Dibya Prabha enacts an immediate, high-priority emergency protocol for endophthalmitis at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care:

methods.name: Rapid Diagnostic Sampling
methods.description: Performing an immediate vitreous tap to extract a sample of the infected fluid, sending it for urgent culture and Gram stain to identify the exact pathogen.

methods.name: Immediate Intravitreal Antibiotics
methods.description: Injecting a potent combination of broad-spectrum antibiotics (such as vancomycin and ceftazidime) directly into the eye to achieve the highest possible drug concentration.

methods.name: Emergency Vitrectomy
methods.description: In severe cases, performing urgent microsurgery to physically remove the infected, pus-filled vitreous gel, clearing toxins and saving the underlying retina.

methods.name: Comprehensive Systemic Therapy
methods.description: Prescribing strong oral or intravenous antibiotics and intensive topical drops to battle the infection on all fronts while closely monitoring the patient's recovery.

whenToSeeDoctor: IMMEDIATELY — if you have severe eye pain with rapidly decreasing vision and redness, especially after recent eye surgery, eye injection, or eye injury. This is a medical emergency; do not wait.
If you notice a white/yellow fluid level in your eye when looking in a mirror
If you have had recent eye surgery and develop new floaters, pain, or decreasing vision
After any penetrating eye injury — seek emergency eye care even if vision seems okay initially

clinicalObservations.standardView: Endophthalmitis is a severe intraocular infection classified as exogenous (post-surgical, post-traumatic) or endogenous. It is an ophthalmic emergency requiring intravitreal antibiotics and often vitrectomy.
clinicalObservations.palamuObservation: Dr. Dibya Prabha at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care manages post-traumatic endophthalmitis from penetrating eye injuries in Jharkhand's agricultural and mining workers — injuries from flying stone chips during mining, thorn penetrations during farming, and metallic foreign bodies from informal welding work without eye protection — that become infected within 24–48 hours.
clinicalObservations.treatmentModification: We perform immediate vitreous tap for culture and Gram stain, administer intravitreal antibiotics (vancomycin + ceftazidime) on presentation, and proceed to vitrectomy within hours rather than days. We counsel workers in Hindi that wearing basic polycarbonate safety glasses costs under Rs. 200 and can prevent a blinding infection.
